# <Behavior or contract>

## Purpose and scope

Link to parent CDDs and state the behavior covered and excluded.

## Terminology and preconditions

Define terms, inputs, assumptions, and preconditions needed to interpret requirements.

## Requirements

Use stable requirement IDs such as `SPEC-NNN-R01`. Describe observable, actionable behavior. Distinguish requirements from examples and rationale.

## Interfaces and data

Define inputs, outputs, types, units, formats, and ownership as applicable. Link to existing canonical schemas instead of duplicating them.

## Edge cases and failures

Specify invalid inputs, errors, boundary cases, and relevant lifecycle transitions.

## Compatibility and invariants

Specify applicable versioning, determinism, cross-language, and compatibility requirements.

## Acceptance criteria and verification

Map requirements to observable checks, expected outcomes, and relevant tests or fixtures. Label planned tests as planned.

| Requirement | Check and expected outcome | Test / fixture reference |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Open questions

Resolve implementation-blocking ambiguity before treating the affected requirements as accepted. If superseded, identify the replacement.
